keys: Assisting walking balance using a bio-inspired exoskeleton controller

papers.locators: Methods: Exoskeleton and controller; Data recording and analysis; reference 45. Bilateral physical series-elastic ankles, 1 kHz control and moment recording, shared analog ground reaction timing reference, rated controlled peak 100 N m.

Section II-B, pp. 332–333: series spring plus separate absolute encoders for joint output, spring deflection and motor angle. Describes the modular device family; individual spring parameters are not assumed for each trial.

evidence_level: Downloaded and CRC-decoded every published subject CSV and compared the shared file SHA-256 to OSF. The CSVs contain both desired and reported applied torque per ankle; the experiment did not include an independently synchronized external joint dynamometer.
scope: 1,054 distinct CSVs from 12 participant codes; 1,381,854 bilateral rows (each side has a finite desired/applied pair in every row). 1,006 short push/pull windows, 48 steady records. The ZIP paths contain NMC_Bal (208 files), which the standalone author README says was not evaluated in the paper. Use trial type and condition to separate these from the published comparison. Subject 9 and 10 were missing per the README.
time_and_units: All signals were interpolated by the authors to 100 Hz. Time 0 marks the platform perturbation onset for push/pull files; steady files have their own local zero. Use same-row reported torque differences in N m on this common grid. Interpolation and synchronization through an analog GRF reference do not yield controller tick or packet timing.
results: All 289 minimal-impedance files (12 steady, 134 pull, 143 push) show zero desired torque at both ankles for all 365,889 published instants. In those windows 547,719 of 731,778 ankle-side records have |applied torque| > 1 N m. Across all conditions the peak |desired| is 50.0 N m and the peak |applied| is 62.900175 N m. Neither exceeds the stated 100 N m peak capability. The data show residual interaction under a zero setpoint; residuals alone do not identify friction, spring-model error or saturation.
statistics: RMSE is the square root of mean squared applied-minus-desired torque. Condition values pool finite ankle-time pairs within condition, trial type and side, weighting each row equally. The 1 N m cut is descriptive; no inference about population or clinical effects. No waveforms are redistributed.
reproduce: Python 3 with pandas and NumPy. Download archive_and_readme[1] (the zip) or the file named Data_NMC_Balance_Ankle.zip.zip; run OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python derive_ankle.py SOURCE_ZIP OUT. Source hash and CSV member CRC are checked; each member digest is in ankle-torque-trials.csv.
